description: FrameCrypto vectors for the VLP v1 link layer: PBKDF2 bootstrap-key derivation, pairing-mode framing (plaintext + outer HMAC), and session-mode framing (AES-256-GCM + outer HMAC). See ProjectInfo/04-PROTOCOL.md section 5.
derivation: Computed with .NET BCL primitives (Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2, AesGcm, HMACSHA256) in a throwaway program referencing neither implementation. .NET's and Java JCE's are separate implementations of the same published standards, so agreement between them is meaningful. The harness was sanity-checked against the published SHA-256 value for 'abc'.

algorithms.bootstrapKey: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(pin, salt, 120000 iterations, 256 bits), salt = min(idA,idB) ':' max(idA,idB) lower-cased, US-ASCII
algorithms.sessionBody: AES-256-GCM, 96-bit nonce, 128-bit tag, body = ciphertext || tag
algorithms.pairingBody: utf8(payloadJson), unencrypted, authenticated by the outer HMAC only

bootstrapKeyVectors.name: PIN 123456, ids ALPHA and bravo
bootstrapKeyVectors.note: The initiator id is given upper-case to pin the lower-casing step. The salt is the ordered pair, so both peers derive the same key regardless of who initiated.

bootstrapKeyVectors.name: Same PIN with the roles reversed derives the identical key
bootstrapKeyVectors.note: This is the whole reason the salt is lexicographically ordered. If this vector fails, pairing succeeds in one direction and fails in the other.

pairingFrameVectors.name: Pairing-mode frame, plaintext body with outer HMAC

sessionFrameVectors.name: Session-mode frame, AES-256-GCM body with outer HMAC
sessionFrameVectors.note: Java's Cipher.doFinal returns ciphertext||tag as a single array; .NET returns them separately. The wire form is the concatenation, so an implementation that keeps them apart must join them in this order.

rejectionVectors.name: A frame whose MAC is altered must not open

input.mutate: flip the last byte of macHex

expected.reason: MAC mismatch, rejected before any decryption is attempted

rejectionVectors.name: A frame re-attributed to a different sender must not open
rejectionVectors.note: This is what binding fromDeviceId into the MAC buys. With a shared key and an unbound MAC, a frame could be lifted and replayed as if it came from another peer.

input.mutate: change fromDeviceId from ALPHA to CHARLIE, leaving nonce, body and mac untouched

rejectionVectors.name: A session frame whose ciphertext is altered must not open

expected.reason: outer HMAC fails first; GCM tag would also fail

rejectionVectors.name: A repeated nonce must be rejected by the replay cache

input.action: open the same valid frame twice

notes: 120000 PBKDF2 iterations is the only thing standing between a 6-digit PIN and an offline attacker who captured the exchange. Lowering it is a security change, not a performance tuning knob.

MAC verification MUST precede decryption and MUST use a constant-time comparison. A short-circuiting compare leaks how many leading tag bytes an attacker guessed, which is enough to forge a tag one byte at a time.
open() must never throw on hostile input; it returns null. A thrown exception that escapes to a connection handler is a denial-of-service lever.
In session mode the outer HMAC is redundant for confidentiality - GCM already authenticates - but it binds the frame to the claimed sender, which GCM does not.
